source.title: Prefrontal circuits signaling active avoidance retrieval and extinction.

confidence_rationale: Retrograde-tracer + c-Fos mapping shows avoidance RETRIEVAL is signaled by prelimbic projections to basolateral amygdala (and to a lesser extent ventral striatum), while extinction recruits IL->BLA/VS and PL->VS. This supports SD-059's architectural premise that a positive avoidance pathway runs through amygdala->ventral-striatum credit projections, distinct from the suppression/extinction route. Correlational (c-Fos), so confidence is moderate.
failure_signatures: Avoidance retrieval did NOT activate IL neurons; the IL route was selective to extinction -- a caution that mapping the SD-059 escape-credit pathway onto IL specifically (as opposed to PL->BLA->VS) would mis-assign the substrate.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Active-avoidance retrieval is signaled by prelimbic (PL) projections to basolateral amygdala (BLA), and PL may modulate ventral striatum (VS) indirectly via BLA; extinction is signaled by infralimbic (IL) projections to BLA and VS plus PL->VS.
mapping.ree_translation: Provides the anatomical scaffold for SD-059's claim that avoidance credit is carried by an amygdala->ventral-striatal (LA/BA->NAcc) action-reinforcement pathway -- the half SD-059 says is UNWIRED to avoidance in current REE. MECH-358's EMA credit table is the functional abstraction of this PL/BLA->VS routing.
mapping.mapping_caveat: c-Fos + tracers establish which projections are ACTIVE during retrieval/extinction, not that they carry a quantitative per-action relief/safety credit; the REE bridge is an arithmetic regulator, so this is substrate-plausibility evidence, not mechanism-identity evidence. The retrieval-vs-extinction dissociation also warns against conflating the IL suppression node with the avoidance-credit node.
mapping.source_context: Male rats; platform-mediated signaled active avoidance; CTB/FluoroGold retrograde tracers into BLA and VS; c-Fos after retrieval (2 tones) vs extinction (15 tones).

confidence_components.notes: Strong anatomy, but correlational activation; rodent->REE arithmetic-regulator transfer risk is the main discount.
